name: D-phenylalanine
short: Safety data are minimal: one 2-week placebo-controlled crossover study in 11 boys noted no side effects (blood phenylalanine rose). A 30-patient pain trial's abstract gives no safety data.
text: The safety evidence found is very limited. In a double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study, 11 boys with hyperactivity took D-phenylalanine for 2 weeks and placebo for 2 weeks; no side effects were noted, there was no significant deterioration in behaviour, and the only measured change was a rise in blood (serum) phenylalanine. In a double-blind crossover trial in 30 people with chronic pain who took D-phenylalanine by mouth for four weeks, the abstract reports only pain outcomes and does not say whether any adverse effects occurred. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
